Implement chunk-level health tracking in the container Merkle tree system of Apache Ozone. Extend the functionality to include a health flag for chunks, support incremental updates from serialized trees, and register an on-demand scanner callback.

*   Modify `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter`:
    *   Update `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo> chunks)` to include a `boolean healthy` parameter. Ensure each `ChunkMerkleTree` entry has `isHealthy` set according to this parameter.
    *   Add a varargs overload `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo... chunks)` to accept multiple `ChunkInfo` instances directly.
    *   Introduce `addBlock(long blockID)` to insert an empty block into the tree without affecting existing entries.
    *   Implement a new constructor `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)` that initializes the writer from an existing proto. Ensure `toProto()` outputs identical to the input proto, including empty blocks.
    *   Ensure the writer remains mutable after initialization from a proto, allowing further updates with `addChunks` or `addBlock`.

*   Update the `ChunkMerkleTree` protobuf message:
    *   Add a `boolean isHealthy` field.
    *   Provide access via `getIsHealthy()` and `setIsHealthy(boolean)` methods.

*   Rename method in `KeyValueHandler`:
    *   Change `createContainerMerkleTree` to `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` to clarify it reads from metadata.
    *   Update all internal call sites to use the new method name.

*   Enhance `ContainerSet`:
    *   Add `registerContainerScanHandler(Function<Container, Optional<Future<?>>> scanHandler)` to allow registration of an on-demand scan handler.
    *   Ensure the handler is invoked automatically during reconciliation to trigger container scans.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the `registerContainerScanHandler` function and related container scanning code in Apache Ozone:

## Background: Why the Scan Handler Was Introduced

The scan handler design emerged from a specific refactoring problem. The on demand container scanner was originally implemented as a static instance so that it could be easily triggered from anywhere in the code. This caused problems for reconciliation testing where multiple replicas exist in the same process, because on-demand scans for each reconciled replica were hitting the same container scanner concurrently.

The solution was described by the developer (errose28): a scan handler was added which can be triggered from the `ContainerSet`. `ContainerSet` was chosen because it is both created by the `OzoneContainer` which also initializes the scanners, and available in most locations in the datanode.

## The `registerContainerScanHandler` Usage

In `OzoneContainer.java`, the scanner is instantiated and its `scanContainer` method is registered as a handler via a method reference: `onDemandScanner = new OnDemandContainerDataScanner(c, controller); containerSet.registerContainerScanHandler(onDemandScanner::scanContainer);`

When asked whether a scanner interface could be used instead, the developer explained the design rationale: preferring to keep the coupling between the two classes looser, noting that a scanner interface would only have one method and only be used there, whereas the consumer was a light-weight way to get this same functionality.

## The `Optional<Future<?>> scanContainer` Signature

The `OnDemandContainerScanner.scanContainer` method returns an `Optional` wrapping a `Future`. Per its Javadoc: it returns an Optional containing a Future representing the pending scan task if the task is queued, and the optional is empty if the task is not queued due to an ongoing scan.

A later change added a scan reason parameter. The method signature evolved from `public Optional<Future<?>> scanContainer(Container<?> container)` to `public Optional<Future<?>> scanContainer(Container<?> container, String reasonForScan)`.

## Related Evolution (HDDS-13423 — Logging Scan Reasons)

A subsequent PR added reason-logging for triggered scans. This changed calls like `containerSet.scanContainerWithoutGap(containerID)` to `containerSet.scanContainerWithoutGap(containerID, "Container reconciliation")`. The commit touched multiple files: ContainerSet.java, HddsDispatcher.java, KeyValueHandler.java, OnDemandContainerScanner.java, ContainerImporter.java, and several test files.

The naming also changed over time — an earlier method `registerOnDemandScanner` was used, as seen where `containerSet.registerOnDemandScanner(onDemandScanner)` appears, and the class `OnDemandContainerDataScanner` was later renamed to `OnDemandContainerScanner`.

## Usage in Test Code

The registration pattern appears in test setup as well, where a `MockDatanode` builds the scanner and wires it to the `ContainerSet`: a `ContainerController` is created, an `OnDemandContainerDataScanner` is instantiated with the scanner configuration, and the on-demand container scanner is registered with the container set used by the KeyValueHandler.

These changes are all part of the broader **HDDS-10239 container reconciliation** effort, with the specific scan-handler refactor tracked under **HDDS-12849** ("On demand container scanner should not be static").

All changes are complete and the module compiles cleanly. Here's a summary of what I implemented:

## Changes

### `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter.java`
- **`addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ChunkInfo>)`** — added the `healthy` parameter; each `ChunkMerkleTree` entry now gets `isHealthy` set from it (instead of always `true`).
- **`addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ChunkInfo... chunks)`** — new varargs overload delegating to the collection form.
- **`addBlock(long blockID)`** — inserts an empty block via `computeIfAbsent`, leaving any existing entry untouched.
- **`ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)`** — new constructor that rebuilds the writer from a proto, reconstructing each chunk (offset, length, `isHealthy`, precomputed `dataChecksum`) and preserving empty blocks. Because chunk data checksums are preserved, `toProto()` reproduces the input proto identically, and the writer stays mutable for further `addChunks`/`addBlock` calls.
- Added a `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter(ChunkMerkleTree)` reconstruction constructor plus `BlockMerkleTreeWriter.addChunk(...)` and a chunk `getOffset()` helper.

### `DatanodeClientProtocol.proto`
- The `ChunkMerkleTree.isHealthy` field (field 4) was already present, so generated `getIsHealthy()`/`setIsHealthy(boolean)` are available and used.

### `KeyValueHandler.java`
- Renamed `createContainerMerkleTree` → `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` and updated all four internal call sites.
- Updated the metadata read path to call `addChunks(localID, true, chunkInfos)` (chunks from metadata are treated as healthy).

### `ContainerSet.java`
- Changed the scan handler field/registration to `Function<Container<?>, Optional<Future<?>>>`, so `registerContainerScanHandler(...)` and `scanContainer(long)` now return the optional scan `Future`. The handler is still invoked from `scanContainer(containerID)`, which the reconciliation flow (`KeyValueHandler.reconcileContainer`) calls, so scans trigger automatically during reconciliation. The `OzoneContainer` registration (`onDemandScanner::scanContainer`) adapts to the new signature unchanged.

I left the `tests/` directory untouched per the instructions.

Sources: [HDDS-12849 discussion](https://www.mail-archive.com/issues@ozone.apache.org/msg111522.html), [HDDS-12980 reconciliation test framework](https://www.mail-archive.com/commits@ozone.apache.org/msg08992.html)
